subject: NaN for S_X2 in Itemfit function

messages.author: eab9582ba50c948a
messages.subject: NaN for S_X2 in Itemfit function
parts:
Hi,

I'm modelling a uniform GRM with 8 items and low N=101. I get good M2 results, but in the itemfit one item's S_X2 is NaN. Is this just due to the low N or does it imply other possible issues?

Here's the console output:

> datWPR.1d <- datWPRclean |> dplyr::select("WPR_7",
+                                           "WPR_8","WPR_9","WPR_10","WPR_11",
+                                           "WPR_12","WPR_15",
+                                           "WPR_17")
> WPR.mirt.1d <- mirt(datWPR.1d, itemtype = "graded", technical = list(NCYCLES = 10000))
Iteration: 46, Log-Lik: -598.358, Max-Change: 0.00010
> (WPR.mirt.1d.fit <- M2(WPR.mirt.1d,type = "C2"))
            M2 df         p     RMSEA RMSEA_5   RMSEA_95      SRMSR       TLI      CFI
stats 20.78055 20 0.4101489 0.0197554       0 0.08874094 0.07292051 0.9924148 0.994582
> (WPR.mirt.1d.itemfit <- itemfit(WPR.mirt.1d))
    item   S_X2 df.S_X2 RMSEA.S_X2 p.S_X2
1  WPR_7  9.047       7      0.054  0.249
2  WPR_8    NaN       0        NaN    NaN
3  WPR_9  2.966       3      0.000  0.397
4 WPR_10 18.365       5      0.163  0.003
5 WPR_11 22.222      14      0.077  0.074
6 WPR_12  7.024       7      0.006  0.426
7 WPR_15  5.143       5      0.017  0.399
8 WPR_17 12.429      12      0.019  0.412

Thanks a lot for your expertise!

Martin

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: NaN for S_X2 in Itemfit function
parts:
Low N combined with sparse expected values will result in 0 df, particularly for polytomous response models. You can adjust the threshold of the expectation collapsing criteria, but in general I would not advise doing this as it can result in very poor p-value behaviour.

Phil
